summary: OpenAI published first performance results for Jalapeño, its custom inference chip, showing higher throughput-per-watt and lower latency than comparison GPU systems across several public models, with plans to begin deploying it in OpenAI's own infrastructure by year end.

mechanisms.reason: OpenAI discloses a working first-party inference chip with measured performance gains and a multigenerational roadmap intended to displace merchant accelerators for inference.
mechanisms.quote: Jalapeño is working first-party silicon with measured results, and it is the beginning of a multigenerational platform.

mechanisms.reason: The chip is stated to deliver substantially more AI work per watt at comparable latency, meaning less hardware/power is required per unit of inference work than on comparison systems.
mechanisms.quote: Across all three, Jalapeño delivered 1.5 to 1.9 times more AI work per watt at peak throughput and 1.7 to 3.6 times lower end-to-end latency than the comparison systems.

mechanisms.reason: OpenAI states the efficiency gains will let it serve more aggregate demand from the same power and hardware.
mechanisms.quote: By producing more useful work from the same power and hardware, Jalapeño can help us serve more demand and lower the cost of delivering a successful result.

categories.reason: OpenAI is deploying its own custom inference accelerator, benchmarked directly against merchant GPU systems (GB200/GB300), signalling substitution of merchant silicon by first-party chips.
categories.quote: Since announcing Jalapeño, OpenAI’s first custom inference chip, we have been testing the chip and the system built around it.

practices.reason: The chip's KV-cache placement and prefill/decode co-design are described concretely but are tied to OpenAI's proprietary silicon and rack-scale system, not something a team could apply on its own stack.
practices.quote: We designed Jalapeño to minimize data movement and communication delays. This means that model state, including the KV cache used while generating a response, can be explicitly placed and kept local while the system activates the right combination of compute, memory, and networking for each inference phase.

practices.reason: OpenAI used a public, third-party benchmark (InferenceX) to measure serving performance, which a team could run to evaluate its own inference systems.
practices.quote: To understand how Jalapeño performs in practice, we tested it on InferenceX, a public benchmark from SemiAnalysis that measures the full process of serving an AI request.

notable_reason: A frontier lab disclosing measured performance results for its first custom inference silicon against Nvidia GB200/GB300 systems is a significant, quantified data point on the custom-silicon substitution trend.
